notes: CONFORMS (2026-11-16; a derivation drafted for this row was OVERTURNED by its refuter, whose program is the row's witness; the record is in the refutations store). §1985:IV.4.4.2 GRL2.2 names a state: "The last statement in a declarative section when the statement is in the range of an active PERFORM statement executed in a different section" and not the last statement of that PERFORM's exit. The state has two parts. (a) A declarative entered by a USE condition while a PERFORM of another section is active: its statements are in that PERFORM's range ("as well as all statements in declarative procedures that are executed as a result of the execution of statements in the range of the PERFORM statement" (§1985:VI.6.21.4 GR11)), and what follows its last statement is fixed by rules of their own: "an implied transfer of control occurs from the last statement in the paragraph to the control mechanism of the last executed controlling statement" (§1985:IV.4.4.2 GR1); "the input-output control system returns control to the next executable statement following the input-output statement whose execution caused the exception" (§1985:VII.4.6.4 GR6); "Return from that procedure is to the next executable statement following the end of the READ statement" (§1985:VII.4.4.4 GR10). The witness runs this part: a READ at end inside a performed section, a declarative that goes to its last paragraph, the return to the statement after the READ, the PERFORM's own exit; a compiler that fell into the next declarative section or ended the PERFORM at the declarative's last statement prints other lines. (b) A declarative paragraph performed from outside that goes to the last paragraph of its section: no rule fixes what follows, and the sentence after the list makes it undefined ("the program flow of control is undefined unless the program execution is in the nondeclarative procedures portion of a program under control of a CALL statement" (§1985:IV.4.4.2 GRL2.5)), so nothing is expected and nothing is witnessed (kb/Work PB5791 records the program; it is not a case). Witness: 1985-GR-IV_4_4_2-L2_2.

next.reason: 1985: "The last statement in a declarative section when the statement is in the range of an active PERFORM statement executed in a different section"; 2023: "In the declarative section for a fatal exception condition, there is no next executable statement after ... the run unit is terminated abnormally". 2023 keeps the no-next-statement case only for fatal-exception declaratives, and now terminates the run unit abnormally, with implementor exceptions for SORT, MERGE and I-O.
